transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-12 14:00 UTC (52 mins)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Everguard Head of ML), Marcus Lee (CTO), Jenna Ortiz (Infra)
---
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining really appreciate you making time. quick agenda — scope the POC, figure out traffic model, define success criteria and timelines. is that right priya?
[00:14] Priya: yeah that's perfect. we're mostly concerned with two things: latency at peak and inference cost, cost per call. we have a set of transaction-analysis prompts that vary a bit, some short ones, some long context ones, maybe up to 2k tokens.
[00:29] Samir (SE): ok great; can you give ballpark numbers on QPS and concurrency? like average QPS, peak QPS, and expected concurrency per instance?
[00:38] Priya: average QPS is about 15, peak is spiky up to 120 QPS during batch windows, concurrency around 40-60 at peak. daily traffic is two spikes — morning batch at 09:30 and end-of-day 17:00 UTC.
[00:56] Marcus (CTO): to add — around 30% of requests are short annotation prompts (~20-60 tokens input, 20-50 tokens output). 50% are full analysis flows with longer inputs (~200-800 input tokens) and outputs averaging 150-400 tokens. rest are embeddings/semantic search calls.
[01:20] Alex: that distribution helps a lot. for modelling we'll want a token histogram — samples for each class. do you have a sample set?
[01:28] Priya: we'll extract 1k prompts this week and annotate. expected by Friday.
[01:34] Samir: good. for the POC we recommend three model variants: 1) LLM-small quantized (cost baseline), 2) LLM-medium with optimized kernels, 3) larger context model for high quality. we'll run the same sample set across all.
[01:49] Jenna: on infra — we need to test both hosted and private routing. currently we prefer private (VPC) for production, but hosted for initial bench. firewall rules and egress IPs needed.
[01:58] Alex: noted. we'll send the network checklist. Jenna, can you share the VPC CIDR and egress needs?
[02:04] Jenna: yes will do, also KMS requirements — we use a customer-managed key for anything hitting production.
[02:10] Alex: we support KMS/HSM integrations; we'll include the SOC2 + key integration notes.
[02:16] Priya: success criteria — for us p95 latency needs to be below 300ms for short prompts and below 800ms for medium/long flows; cost per call target is TBD after you give initial numbers but we'd like a delta vs our current costs. accuracy/regression: we need <2% top-level regression on extraction F1 for the sample set.
[02:36] Samir: quick clarifying question — when you say 800ms for medium flows, is that end-to-end or just decode?
[02:41] Priya: end-to-end, including network.
[02:44] Samir: ok we'll report both SLOs and network-excluded numbers. Redwood's dedicated pools can usually hit lower decode latency; hosted adds network overhead.
[02:53] Marcus: are you able to simulate the concurrent KV cache patterns? we use prefix caching heavily for repeated customer-context lookups.
[03:01] Samir: yes, we can emulate K V cache warm ups and cold-start behaviour in the benchmark harness. note — the transcription may show K V cash sometimes, haha.
[03:10] (laughter)
[03:15] Alex: on throughput — given your peak 120 QPS and concurrency ~50, realistic modelling suggests we should test sustained 120 QPS for a 30-60 minute window plus diurnal pattern for 24h to capture cache behavior. that will surface batching efficiency and token throughput impacts.
[03:29] Priya: that sounds right. what's the typical batch size you'd see at that QPS?
[03:33] Samir: depends on arrival distribution; if requests are bursty we get larger batches, which increases throughput but latency tail can worsen. for example for medium model we might see batches of 8-32 tokens per micro-batch, overall effective batch size per GPU 64-256 depending on shard.
[03:49] Alex: also we'll capture cost per token and cost per successful inference for your workload. we'll run a cost/latency tradeoff table across quantization and batching configs.
[03:58] Marcus: what about large context flows — some prompts go up to 2k input tokens and expect 512 token outputs. that's heavy. can Redwood support 8k context models?
[04:08] Samir: we have runtime paths for longer context (we call out kernel selection and chunked KV caching). for the POC we'll benchmark both 2k and a fall-back 8k config; note costs scale roughly linearly with context length for memory and KV ops.
[04:22] Priya: for our success criteria long flows can be lower priority; priority is short and medium flows.
[04:29] Alex: agreed. proposed POC plan: 1) week 1 — exchange samples + network info, 2) week 2 — Redwood runs initial 24h benchmark (3 variants) capturing p50/p95 latency, throughput, token distribution, cost per 1k requests, and regression metrics vs annotated labels, 3) week 3 — review results and decide next steps (pilot or dedicated sizing). does that timeline work?
[04:50] Priya: yes except we may need an extra day to scrub sensitive data — we'll provide anonymized prompts.
[04:55] Alex: fine, anonymized is fine. we'll give the template to map classes (short/medium/long/embedding).
[05:02] Jenna: about private testing — we want to run a small pilot in our VPC, ideally during the initial benchmark to validate egress and latency. any blockers here?
[05:10] Samir: we'll need your firewall rules and will coordinate a short window for VPC peering or allowlist. private testing adds some ops overhead but is doable mid-benchmark.
[05:19] Marcus: what measurements will you provide? we need traces, token-level cost breakdown, route-level latency breakdown.
[05:26] Alex: we'll deliver a benchmark report with p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, per-model cost delta, batch/kv hit rates, and a CSV of raw results. we'll also provide recommended configs for Dedicated sizing.
[05:37] Priya: any gotchas?
[05:39] Samir: watch out for tail latency with batching when you have heterogeneous token lengths; we'll run synthetic mixes to surface tail. also quantization can reduce cost but sometimes hurts extractive accuracy slightly; we'll measure regression on your F1 metric.
[05:53] Alex: ok quick recap of action items and owners (see meeting notes). we'll follow up with the workload template and a proposed benchmark schedule. thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the initial run.
[06:03] Priya: thanks all.
---
